blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content: Classical (non-neutral) Tannaka's duality over a field $k$ establishes a correspondence between $k$-Tannakian categories and affine gerbes over $k$. blocks.title: Notation
blocks.content:
In this paper we work over a base commutative, associative ring $R$ with unity. If not stated otherwise a fiber category will be a category fibered in groupoids over $\mathop{\mathrm{\textup{Aff}}}/R$, the category of affine schemes over $\mathop{\mathrm{\textup{Spec}}}R$, or, equivalently, the opposite of the category of $R$-algebras. An fpqc stack will be a stack for the fpqc topology.

A map $f\colon\stX'\arr\stX$ of fibered categories is called representable if for all maps $T\arr\stX$ from an affine scheme (or an algebraic space) the fiber product $T\times_{\stX}\stX'$ is (equivalent to)

blocks.title: Pseudo-affine stacks
blocks.content:
One of the key points in the proof of Theorem [\[thma\]](#thma){reference-type="ref" reference="thma"} is a characterization of the following stacks.

::: defn
A *pseudo-affine* stack is a quasi-compact fpqc stack with quasi-affine diagonal such that all quasi-coherent sheaves on it are generated by global sections. In other words a pseudo-affine stack is a quasi-compact fpqc stack $\stX$ such that $\{\odi{\stX}\}$ generates $\mathop{\mathrm{\textup{QCoh}}}(\stX)$.
